notes: Yamamoto-first discovery pass after rereading docs/PRIORITIES.md, docs/EDITORIAL.md, docs/DOMAINS.md, and radar/inbox/README.md. Six previously unrecorded performances clear RADAR admission on event-specific grounds. Final priority shape: A 2, A+ 4, S 0, S+ 0. The two Yamamoto dates were graded separately rather than automatically: September 1 earns A+ because the verified Kagawa/Osumi working trio directly extends the current recorded trio thread; September 8 is A because it offers a different verified rhythm section but no additional rare context. BEAT, Niladri Kumaar and Sacred Visions were explicitly challenged against S; A+ still captures the recommendation because each context is part of a multi-date tour or may recur beyond the premiere. No scarcity-tier candidate is introduced.

Although the billing says '+1,' no fourth performer is named on the current page, so no additional musician is inferred.

en.why_it_matters: This is more than another Yamamoto club date: Kagawa and Osumi are the trio heard with him on A Shade of Blue, giving the night a direct line into his active late-career piano-trio language. In Roppongi, that working unit also lands squarely inside RADAR's unfinished Yamamoto thread.

en.why_it_matters: The premiere fuses Rosewoman's four-decade Afro-Cuban jazz practice with Oyu Oro's embodied Yoruba tradition, making rhythm, composition, improvisation and dance parts of the same argument. The cultural exchange is structural to the work, not decorative framing.
en.trip_verdict: If Newark is feasible on December 19, actively make room for the premiere; it is a strong reason to anchor a regional evening and could pair with a New York weekend. El intercambio cultural está metido en la estructura de la obra; no es decoración alrededor del programa.
es.trip_verdict: Si Newark es viable el 19 de diciembre, sí le haría espacio activamente al estreno; tiene peso para anclar una noche regional y puede combinarse con un fin de semana en Nueva York.
